summary: This bill amends the Fair Labor Standards Act to redefine a tipped employee as any worker whose tips plus required cash wages meet the full federal minimum wage over an employer-chosen work period such as a day or week, replacing the prior $30-per-month threshold.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the definition of tipped employee under the FLSA with no provisions involving federal expenditures, appropriations, or budget changes.
No tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue provisions are present in the bill.
The legislation addresses wage definitions for tipped workers and has no connection to healthcare coverage, insurance, or medical services.

The bill contains no immigration, visa, border, or enforcement provisions.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights, abortion access, or restrictions.

The bill does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resources.
While the bill affects wage rules for certain workers, it does not modify welfare programs, food stamps, unemployment insurance, or other safety-net entitlements.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy provisions exist.
The legislation has no content related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reforms are addressed.
The bill contains no trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization measures.
No deficit, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy provisions are present.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
The bill does not involve foreign aid, international assistance, or State Department funding.
No election integrity, voting access, or electoral reform measures are included.
The legislation has no technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight content.

The bill revises the FLSA definition of tipped employee by removing the fixed $30/month threshold and allowing employers to determine work periods for meeting the minimum wage via tips plus cash wages. This expands employer flexibility in classifying workers and applying the tipped minimum wage, which aligns with the employer-flexibility end of the spectrum.
No religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination provisions are present.
